{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZjNEQA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDJ76I", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 71, "title": "Correct V30MZ LOOP, LOOPE and LOOPNE timing and affected probe budgets", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `995741d92168ee7156cb8d853ac86d244714bf19`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:670–686` gives E0–E2 the same execution charge: 4 clocks taken and 1 otherwise. It also omits the taken odd-target penalty. Ordinary loop and polling budgets therefore advance video, timers, audio and DMA too quickly. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

The existing semantic LOOP test checks results without timing. The IRQ timing fixture and its native/browser consumers also embed the old LOOP cost.

## Expected outcome

Correct E2 LOOP and E0/E1 LOOPNE/LOOPE timing within the existing serialized CPU accounting, preserving architectural results and charging actual instruction fetches once. Include necessary tests, fixtures, consumers and documentation changes.

Keep JCXZ, JMP, other instruction timing, full prefetch and external-bus policy as separate work.

## Context

Local HEAD and inspected remote main match the baseline; the checkout is clean. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. All 70 closed entry titles were checked without finding an equivalent completed task.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), Appendix A conditions/Note 5 and Table A-1 (printed pp. 73, 77), specifies decoded execution costs of 5/2 clocks for DBNZ (E2) and 6/3 for DBNZE/DBNZNE (E1/E0), taken/fallthrough respectively, plus one clock when branching to an odd address. These register-only instructions have no operand transfer to subtract. Under the repository's two explicit internal byte fetches, inferred step totals are 7/4 and 8/5 respectively, with one additional clock only for taken odd targets.

Correction record: the old AI-authored assumption was that shared 4/1 execution costs and the IRQ harness's LOOP 6/3 totals were suitable. Replace it with instruction-specific execution costs, explicit fetch accounting and the applicable target penalty. The primary table distinguishes these instructions. Record any further evidence-backed correction with its old assumption, replacement, source and rationale; preserve relevant acceptance without introducing an approval gate.

The [timing experiment report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSTimingTest/blob/025e606fc3b6615160ffdae485d992ffcad0c024/README.md) corroborates odd-target effects but explicitly qualifies aggregate harness/pipeline results. Its opcode-pattern workaround is unsuitable. Full console pipeline accuracy remains unresolved.

Inspection of `fixtures/irq-timing.asm` and committed cartridge bytes establishes that its measured LOOP targets `0x2005`. With that layout unchanged, 1023 taken iterations gain two clocks each and the final fallthrough gains one: the documented 59412/65556-clock budgets become 61459/67603, giving 240–241/264–265 HBlank ticks. These are calculated expectations, not observed results.

Preserve [Issue #69](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/69)'s IRQ-entry and integration acceptance. Its [saved validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/995741d92168ee7156cb8d853ac86d244714bf19/docs/issue-69-validation.md) reports 232 workspace tests and complete production Chromium suites passing with the previous harness budget. Tests and reports were inspected; this investigation ran no builds or tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the instruction-specific accounting and independent literal vectors before changing timing. Implement E0–E2 costs and taken-target parity handling without speculative prefetch or bus changes. Count fetches, waits, interrupt entry and DMA stalls separately and exactly once.
- [ ] Add native vectors for all three opcodes: taken/fallthrough, both ZF values, incoming CX values 0/1/2/FFFF, decrement wrap, forward/backward displacements, even/odd targets and IP wrapping. Assert complete preserved FLAGS, CX, CS/IP and untouched registers/memory. Use literal expected costs rather than production timing helpers; internal totals must match the Context derivation. Cover mapped ROM fetches and existing width/wait controls, retaining prefix and E3 behavior.
- [ ] Exercise emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations: Mono mode 00; Color and SwanCrystal modes 00/80/C0/E0, including runtime transitions. Add normal `Machine::run_frame` boundary checks showing the corrected instruction advances raster/frame state, timers and audio once, without an extra application instruction. Preserve IRQ/TF arbitration, shadows, REP/HALT and separate GDMA/SDMA scheduling and gates.
- [ ] Add or extend an original source-included CC0 cartridge with independent native and production Chromium consumers covering all three LOOP opcodes and absolute timing observations. Check CPU-written counts, destinations/continuation and timing on every supported model/mode and fresh restart. Invalidate stale save completion. Record an actual failure with the old LOOP implementation and corrected native/browser passes; a relative alignment delta alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Recalculate affected existing timing oracles, including `docs/external-irq-timing.md`, `crates/ws-core/tests/irq_timing.rs` and `web/scripts/irq-timing.mjs`. For the unchanged IRQ fixture use the derived budgets above; document independent recalculation if its layout changes. Preserve IRQ entry at 32/35 internal clocks, handler counts 1024/0/0, restart/stale-save checks and discrimination against the former IRQ charge. Do not widen tolerances to absorb failures or rewrite historical observations as new passes.
- [ ] Preserve firmware-free startup, three-model behavior, LCD/input/frame continuity, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/cartridge/internal EEPROM and RTC retention, browser save integrity, local data handling and ownership/provenance. Coordinator runs `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against an explicit production preview.
- [ ] Update timing documentation, fixture provenance and validation evidence with tested source/artifact identities, actual observations, failures, corrections and unperformed checks. Coordinator reviews the final diff and evidence against every criterion and resolves blocking findings before merge.

## Optional validation

Additional lawful software timing experiments, browser engines, console comparisons and human gameplay may provide evidence. They were unperformed during planning and are not prerequisites. Mandatory acceptance needs no proprietary ROMs or firmware.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
